stem: Spot USD/GBP is 1.2600 (US dollars per pound). The 90-day USD interest rate is 5.0% and the 90-day GBP interest rate is 4.0%, both quoted on a 360-day basis. The 90-day forward USD/GBP rate implied by covered interest rate parity is closest to:
explanation: F = 1.2600 × (1 + 0.05 × 90/360) / (1 + 0.04 × 90/360) = 1.2600 × 1.0125 / 1.0100 = 1.2631. The pound has the lower rate, so it trades at a forward premium.

rationale.A: Incorrect. 1.2569 puts the GBP rate in the numerator and the USD rate in the denominator; the price-currency (USD) rate belongs on top.
rationale.C: Incorrect. 1.2721 uses the full annual rates (1.05/1.04) without scaling by 90/360.

stem: A hedge fund borrows Swiss francs for one year at 1.0% and invests the proceeds in Mexican peso deposits yielding 10.0%. Over the year the peso depreciates 6% against the franc. The fund's carry trade return, measured in francs on the borrowed amount, is closest to:

rationale.A: Incorrect. 3.00% is the linear approximation 10 − 1 − 6, which ignores the cross term (the 6% loss also applies to the interest earned).
rationale.B: Incorrect. 9.00% is the interest differential only and ignores the peso's depreciation.

stem: A country with highly mobile capital announces a large fiscal stimulus while its central bank simultaneously raises policy rates to fight inflation. According to the Mundell-Fleming model, the short-run effect on its currency is most likely:
explanation: Both policies push domestic interest rates up. With high capital mobility, capital flows in strongly, so the currency appreciates sharply.

rationale.A: Correct. Expansionary fiscal plus restrictive monetary policy raises interest rates, attracting capital inflows under high mobility.
rationale.B: Incorrect. Strong depreciation follows the opposite mix: expansionary monetary with restrictive fiscal policy.
rationale.C: Incorrect. The effect is ambiguous only when fiscal and monetary policy push in the same direction on demand (both expansionary or both restrictive); here both raise rates.

stem: A dealer quotes USD/EUR at 1.0800 - 1.0802 and JPY/USD at 150.20 - 150.25. The offer side of the JPY/EUR cross rate is closest to:

rationale.A: Incorrect. 162.25 multiplies the USD/EUR offer by the JPY/USD bid, mixing sides.
rationale.B: Incorrect. 162.27 multiplies the USD/EUR bid by the JPY/USD offer, mixing sides.
